body:
During #152/#153 validation on L40, Warp1.19.0, CUDA12.9/driver570.158.01, unfiltered padded Compute Sanitizer with the existing128KiB diagnostic stack runs the full mesher tests very slowly in a shared process. The first cube and torus cases finish; the cavity case remains at device synchronization. After30m34s total, the run was interrupted deliberately. Pytest reports2passed, KeyboardInterrupt at `warp/_src/context.py:12720` (`wp_cuda_context_synchronize`), and the sanitizer reports0errors. This is an INCOMPLETE run, not a pass or an established memory defect.

The identical cavity test in a fresh instrumented process passes in36.48s with0errors. Normal full-suite validation already passes633tests;89surface/sampling padded memory tests pass with0errors. The affected complete-mesher cases are being rerun individually with timed Python stack diagnostics. A bounded baseline mixed-process control is pending.

Track the interaction without attributing it prematurely to either Warpower or the tooling:
- [x] Complete isolated coverage of all selected full-mesher cases and preserve the interrupted log.
- [x] Run the preceding runtime under the same mixed-process sequence with timed stack diagnostics.
- [ ] Reduce the combination of live/cached graphs, allocator state and synchronization; compare diagnostic settings without changing production policy.
- [x] Preserve native capture and ordinary changing-input/outer-loop checks.

Related #147 (mixed graph/stack-sensitive instrumentation failure) and #91 (isolated conditional radix-sort allocation-order diagnostics). Neither relationship establishes a shared root cause. No runtime workaround or weakened geometry check is authorized by this issue.

Completed follow-up: all six selected full-mesher tests pass in fresh instrumented processes with zero errors, including changing-input recovery (315.85 s) and the outer device-controlled loop (56.77 s). The preceding runtime `18b18f5` also exceeds the 120-second per-test watchdog during `SiteHierarchy.__init__` at `wp.synchronize_device`, after one completed case (178.18 s total, exit 1, zero reported sanitizer errors). This baseline control is incomplete, not a pass; it shows that the delay also occurs without the new surface hierarchy, but does not identify its cause.

Pool-disabled surface lifetime/API checks and both strict native graph audits pass. Full-solve and changing-input traces each contain three launches and one final synchronization; graphs contain no host transfers/callbacks/allocations/frees. All raw records are being published with PR #153 under `results/validation/vtm/surface-radix`. The unresolved reduction remains tracked here.
title: Investigate synchronization delay in combined full-mesher sanitizer runs
